claim.pdf_says: E.3.3   Not affecting  [a third-level clause, printed in exactly the same style and at the same level as E.3.1 General and E.3.2 Possibly affecting because of the addition of new words or names]
claim.markdown_says: ## E.3.3 Not affecting  (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 48946) -- while its siblings are '### E.3.1 General' (line 48907) and '### E.3.2 Possibly affecting because of the addition of new words or names' (line 48912)
claim.why_it_matters: E.3.3 is transcribed one heading level too shallow, so in the outline it is a sibling of its own parent E.3 ('## E.3 Substantive changes probably not affecting existing programs', line 48904) instead of a child alongside E.3.1 and E.3.2. Everything under E.3.3 - the bulk of Annex E's 'not affecting' catalogue, including the whole user-defined-word character list on pages 1213-1222 - is detached from E.3 in any structural traversal of the document.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED. Nothing is missing and no text differs; the sole difference is the markdown '#' count, and that count is mechanical page-break furniture - one of the enumerated rejection criteria.

(1) The heading is PRESENT and verbatim correct. Rendered PDF p.1212 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1212/spec_p1212.png) prints 'E.3.3   Not affecting' in bold, immediately after item '6) SYNCHRONIZED clause' and immediately before item '1) The ANYCASE keyword of the NUMVAL-C function'. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 48946 reads '## E.3.3 Not affecting', in exactly that position between the same two items. Clause number, title, and placement all match. The kind label 'missing-heading' misdescribes the finding - the heading is not missing, its markdown depth marker differs.

(2) The PDF offers no typographic level signal to lose. On rendered p.1211 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1211/spec_p1211.png), 'E.3 Substantive changes probably not affecting existing programs', 'E.3.1 General' and 'E.3.2 Possibly affecting because of the addition of new words or names' are printed in ONE identical bold serif style, same size, same left margin - ISO uses a single heading style and expresses level solely through the clause number. 'E.3.3' on p.1212 is that same single style. The level is carried by the digits 'E.3.3', which the markdown transcribes correctly inside the heading text. So the authoritative hierarchy encoding is preserved.

(3) The depth is assigned PER PAGE by the transcription pipeline, not per document - proven mechanically. The first clause heading after every '## Page NNNN' marker is emitted at '##' and deeper ones on the same page get '###'/'####':
  - line 48887 '## Page 1211' -> 48904 '## E.3' -> 48907 '### E.3.1' -> 48912 '### E.3.2'
  - line 48927 '## Page 1212' + 48929 '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' -> 48946 '## E.3.3'
  - line 48502/48511 '## Page 1202' -> 48516 '## Annex E' -> 48522 '### E.1' -> 48527 '### E.2'
The same artifact recurs throughout Annex D, each instance immediately preceded by a page marker: 41529 '## Page 1036' -> 41534 '## D.2.2.2'; 41544 '## Page 1037' -> 41549 '## D.2.2.3'; 41623 '## Page 1039' -> 41628 '## D.2.3.2.3'; 41692 '## Page 1041' -> 41697 '## D.2.3.3.3'. It even promotes ordinary numbered LIST ITEMS to '##' when they lead a page ('## 5) **Characters permitted in user-defined words.**' on p.1213, '## 6) **General case mappings.**' on p.1222). E.3.3 is at '##' for exactly one reason: it is the first heading on page 1212. That is page-break furniture.

(4) The stated impact is factually false. The claim asserts the content is 'detached from E.3 in any structural traversal'. But the transcription emits a LEVEL-1 heading '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' as the running head at every page break - 941 occurrences document-wide, including line 48929 between E.3.2 and E.3.3, and again on each of pages 1213-1222. A level-1 heading closes every open section, so E.3 is already severed at the 1211/1212 boundary and re-severed on all ten character-list pages regardless of E.3.3's depth. Changing '##' to '###' on line 48946 would reattach nothing. Heading-depth traversal is not a supported structure in this transcription at all.

(5) The claim singles out E.3.3 from a globally page-relative depth assignment. E.3 itself sits at '##' while its true siblings E.1 and E.2 sit at '###' (lines 48522, 48527). 'Sibling of its own parent' is a restatement of the same furniture artifact, not a defect localized to E.3.3.

No word, character, clause number, item number, or normative statement of ISO/IEC 1989:2023 differs between the PDF page and the markdown. Nothing about COBOL syntax or semantics is affected. Not a content discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a page-1212 content discrepancy. The E.3.3 heading is present with correct clause number, correct title, and correct position; only the markdown '#' depth differs, and that depth is assigned relative to the page by the OCR/conversion pipeline - the first heading after each '## Page NNNN' marker is always emitted at '##'. If the project wants to ledger anything here, it is ONE global pipeline item, not a per-page finding: (a) heading depth resets at every page boundary, flattening the first clause heading on each page (and sometimes a numbered list item) to '##' - hundreds of instances across Annexes D and E and the rest of the document; and (b) the running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' is emitted as a LEVEL-1 heading 941 times, which by itself makes markdown heading depth unusable for structural traversal anywhere in specs/ISO_COBOL.md. Consumers needing Annex hierarchy should parse the clause number in the heading text, which is transcribed correctly.
